subject.title: fix(coding-agent): scope CODEX_HOME to prevent OAuth collision with OpenClaw

question: Should bundled coding-agent Codex launches intentionally reset existing ambient Codex settings by default in exchange for deterministic OAuth isolation?
rationale: The technically safe OAuth boundary changes an existing worker's effective models, providers, MCP servers, hooks, skills, and plugins, so repository policy requires an owner to accept or revise that upgrade behavior.

options.title: Approve a safer clean profile
options.body: Keep the isolated empty worker home, replace wholesale config copying with selective audited migration guidance, and require live upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve selected settings automatically
options.body: Design and test a sanitizer that transfers approved non-secret settings without copying auth or credential-bearing configuration.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Leave the ambient launch instructions unchanged until the coding-agent ownership and migration policy has a supported implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve a safer clean profile
recommendation.body: Keep the isolated empty worker home, replace wholesale config copying with selective audited migration guidance, and require live upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current skill history shows the broadest and longest-running ownership of its launch and safety policy.
